To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a crosslinked collagen gel provides an appropriate substrate for the formation of hemidemsosomes, basal lamina and anchoring fibril structures in a corneallike tissue explant outgrowth model.

crosslinked collagen gel coatings provide a collagenous matrix for the development of epithelial adhesive structure and that this coating method is suitable for the development of corneal tissue constructs.
the architecture of the collagen coating on a microporous polystyrene surface influences corneal epithelium adhesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a synthetic polymer that can be used as a corneal substitute.
the development of a collagen coating method to provide an adhesive surface for polymer-based ocular prostheses.

the development of a collagen coating methodology that provides for the development of epithelial adhesive structure formation at the tissue-penetrating surface of the coating, which is necessary for the development of an adhesive polymer scaffold for corneal regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the collagen coating methodology that provides a crosslinked collagen gel on a microporous surface is the optimal method for supporting the formation of adhesive structures between corneal epithelium and synthetic polymer substrates.

the collagen coating method that provided a crosslinked gel of collagen on a polymer surface allowed for the formation and maintenance of adhesive structures that supported the overlying corneal epithelium.

the collagen coating of a synthetic polymer surface with a crosslinked gel of collagen I provides a substrate that supports the adhesion of cornea epithelial cells in vitro and that the collagen gel coating is a promising approach for the development of a tissue engineering scaffold for the treatment of corneal wounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a crosslinked collagen gel coating provides a suitable collagen matrix for corneal epithelium attachment and growth.
a collagen gel coating on a synthetic surface provides for the development of an adhesive structure that supports corneal epithelium.
a collagen gel coating of polymer surfaces is an effective approach for promoting the formation of a basement membrane at the tissue-particle interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a crosslinked collagen coating can support corneal tissue outgrowth and that it can be used as a substrate to develop adhesive structures.
the architecture of the collagen coating on a polymer surface is a critical factor in the development of an adhesive interface between epithelium and the polymer surface.

collagen coating of synthetic surfaces can be optimized to provide the appropriate architecture for epithelial tissue adhesion and that this architecture may be influenced by the method of collagen immobilization.
